findings.finding: Final forward-wave planning retained forward direction, shoulder height, straight arms, and waving, but did not explicitly require that forward extension and elbow straightness persist throughout the wave.
Correction requesting horizontal extension yielded side extension and a hold; the prior wave requirement was dropped in that refinement.
Later straight-arm correction yielded forward hold, dropping the earlier wave requirement. That may help isolate the pose but is not the full cumulative requested action.

The final follow-up was a new generated motion approximately 19.795 seconds after the previous hold started; the previous 6-second action had completed and the controller returns to Animator idle. The interface does not preserve the last requested pose indefinitely for a later command.
findings.evidence: response-26 started 07:14:41.5418617Z; response-28 started 07:15:01.3369250Z; both completed; controller normal completion/idle behavior

findings.finding: No final basic-wave routing or duplicate command was observed. The inspected correction motions dispatched generate exactly once for generations 18, 22, 24, 26 and 28.
All eight traces received three HTTP 200 windows totaling 120 frames. Seven completed; response-18 was canceled by user speech near 5.66 seconds. Final response-28 completed normally.

recommendations: Treat user refinements as updates to the cumulative action goal: retain unrevoked constraints such as side, coordinate direction, height, elbow extension, ongoing motion, and ordering.
Use a basic gesture only when it represents the entire requested action. A named gesture with added pose, bilateral, timing, or hold constraints should remain an open-ended generated description.
Distinguish obtaining a posture from maintaining it during another motion; express simultaneous posture constraints and moving body parts explicitly, without hardcoding a named action.

Separate desired action context from measured current pose. After completion or cancellation, regenerate the complete intended action from the current measured pose; never claim a preceding pose is still held.
Keep barge-in cancellation. If persistent pose continuation is added later, make it explicit in runtime state/contracts and evaluate entry, held pose, overlay motion and interruption separately.

Compare original and constraint-preserving descriptions with identical seed/history and teacher versus adapter; measure forward reach, elbow extension and actual oscillation jointly over time, plus actual VRM review. Do not tune on the frozen final generalization suite.
limits: Text/log evidence locates planning and lifecycle weaknesses but cannot prove that wording alone fixes the motion generator.
Naturalness and composite-action success require time-series/actual mesh review; HTTP completion does not establish semantic success.
